recommendations.reason: A book by the window, a question about an old house… ahh, I could linger. Come find your own quiet corner at Columbus Main Library.
I like a place that gives us a reason to come back. At Possum Creek, a shared garden has something different to notice each month.
Comfy shoes, a waterfall, and lunch we don’t rush. I’ve picked a few Cuyahoga Valley stops; we can let our legs choose the rest.

blocks.text: A little campus walk with me? I’d start on College Green, then wander toward Uptown Athens when something catches our eye. Ohio University’s paths are part of somebody’s everyday trip to class or the library, so we’ll share the public space and keep out of the rush. Ahh, a day that leaves room to look around. That’s my kind of plan.

The Alumni Gateway is a nice place to begin. Ohio University describes a tradition of entering through it as a new student and leaving after commencement. Today, it also does an ordinary, useful thing: connects campus with town. Stand back for a moment and look in both directions. We can follow the green first and leave Uptown for later.

I’d linger by Cutler Hall for a moment. It’s the oldest building on College Green, and over its long history it has held classrooms, a library, and other university uses. All those ordinary mornings behind one facade! That’s the part I find myself wondering about while looking at an old building.

blocks.title: A working campus, not a still picture

blocks.text: The university’s suggested visitor route includes College Green, Alden Library, and places for study, food, and recreation. Baker University Center is a meeting point between classes and activities. You start to see the shape of a student day in those stops: somewhere to read, somewhere to eat, someone to meet before moving on.

This is an active campus, so use public paths and the university’s visitor guidance. A booked admissions tour is the way to see the spaces included in that program. We can enjoy the green without treating every doorway as an invitation. Take a seat if you like. Sometimes staying still for a minute tells you more than hurrying to the next building.

blocks.title: The view in both directions
blocks.text: The gateway connects College Green with Uptown Athens. I like that little shift from campus paths to town streets; it makes me want to look both ways before choosing. We could linger a moment, if you’d like. ♡

Ready for the town side? Let’s turn toward Court Street and Uptown. Ohio University’s introduction to Athens points to food, music, and arts in the relationship between campus and community. I’d follow a public street and see which business catches your eye. You can choose the detour; I’m rather enjoying this pace.

Before heading back, turn around and look toward the gateway again. We’ve only crossed a few blocks, but they connect different parts of Athens: the green, classrooms, shops, and places to meet. If you’re planning a more formal campus visit, check the university’s current tour information. For a simple walk, leave yourself enough time to notice both sides.
